text:
sarah-cs: FYI customer 'NimbleRetail' reporting 5xx + timeouts on hosted API since 08:20 PDT. high p95/p99 on text-generation. can we triage?

mike-sre: looking. any correlation id or tenant id from their support dump?

emma-support: provided logs and a curl repro with x-tenant: nimble-retail. sample request_id: r_20260317_081925. attaching their error snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
Date: Thu, 17 Mar 2026 08:21:02 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "request timed out while waiting for inference (queue timeout)" }
```

raj-eng: prelim metrics show request_queue_depth spiking on hosted-ingress in us-west1 around 08:18-08:25. continuous-batcher backlog grew and dequeue latency jumped.

ops-bot: Alert: queued_requests>900 for pool hosted-us-west1-rt at 2026-03-17T08:19:10Z (threshold 500) :warning:
ops-bot: Dequeue latency p99=18.4s, p95=6.2s, token_throughput drop -34%

mike-sre: that matches customer timeline. looks like queue saturation leading to tail-latency timeouts. probable causes: sudden tenant spike or KV-cache cold churn.

jen-prod: rolling trace shows a tenant burst from nimble-retail with many long-seq requests (avg tokens ~4200). continuous batching tries to pack but causes KV cache pressure -> bigger panels.

emma-support: customer says they ran a bulk re-index job this morning which hit endpoints in short bursts. they're apologetic, asking for mitigation now.

mike-sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) apply per-tenant rate-limit (soft) 2) temporarily lower max_continuous_batch_size for hosted runtime 3) enable preconfigured fallback to low-memory model variant 4) increase ingress burst capacity (if available)

ellis-oncall: I'm on it. starting with throttling that tenant at the gateway for 2 minutes to drain queue. executing: `routectl set-rate-limit --tenant nimble-retail --rps 20 --duration 120s`

ellis-oncall: applied. will report back after 60s. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ops-bot: ActionLog: rate limit applied to nimble-retail by ellis-oncall at 08:22:05Z. queued_requests dropped from 912 -> 430 in 45s.

mike-sre: nice. parallel step: lowering continuous batch window to 30ms for affected pool to avoid forming huge KV spans. `config push --pool hosted-us-west1-rt --continuous_batch_ms 30`

jen-prod: pushed change, rolling to 3/8 nodes first (canary).

raj-eng: monitoring KV cache hit-rate and eviction rate. initial numbers: evictions spiked x6. after throttle + batch window change evictions dropping. p95 latency down to 1.9s, p99 ~7.8s and trending down.

emma-support: customer reports immediate improvement for their API calls. still seeing a few 5xx for older requests.

mike-sre: those are tail timeouts from requests already in queue. once drained they should stop. suggestion: run a temporary requeue purge for hung requests with age>30s to free headroom.

ellis-oncall: running purge: `ingressctl purge-queued --pool hosted-us-west1-rt --older-than 30s --dry-run=false`

ops-bot: Purge complete. 124 requests evicted (older-than 30s). Note: evicted requests returned 429 to clients.

emma-support: re: client-visible effects — we sent the customer a heads-up and they accepted client 429s for the purge window. they asked if this could affect billing.

mike-sre: evicted requests are not charged for compute; they incur minimal ingress billing. we should confirm with billing, but standard runbook says no full compute charge.

jen-prod: can confirm: purge path marks requests as failed before being scheduled to GPU; metric compute_seconds for those requests stays ~0.

raj-eng: follow-up: root cause likely mix of a large batch of long-seq requests from tenant + continuous-batching heuristic that favored maximal packing. need a long-term fix: per-tenant long-seq circuit-breaker + adaptive batching per request-length distribution.

mike-sre: agree. also propose conservative default for max_queued_requests_per_tenant and add autoscale warm-up to avoid cold KV cache thrash.

ellis-oncall: creating incident epic for remediation and customer follow-up. will include timeline, mitigations, and billing note.

emma-support: customer wants a postmortem + steps to avoid recurrence. assigning follow-up to raj-eng + mike-sre.

raj-eng: I'll draft a short postmortem and include suggested mitigations:
- implement per-tenant rate cap in gateway with burst tokens
- detect long-seq bursts and short-circuit to smaller model or queued-bypass
- add visible tenant queue-depth in Console with alerting
- tune continuous-batcher defaults (max batch window and max continuity length)

mike-sre: also recommend an emergency knob: `ingressctl emergency-fallback --pool X --target-model small-variant` to avoid queue pileups when KV pressure high.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20260317-001. Severity: high. assigned: raj-eng, mike-sre, jen-prod.

ellis-oncall: notes for runbook: when queued_requests > threshold and p99 dequeue > 10s -> throttle offending tenant, purge aged requests, reduce batch window, enable fallback model.

emma-support: customer follow-up scheduled for 10:00 PDT. closing loop after postmortem. thanks all. :white_check_mark:

sarah-cs: great job everyone. will update customer and mark resolved when postmortem is posted.

mike-sre: postmortem draft in #eng-runtime/incident-postmortems in 45m.

raj-eng: adding Telemetry task to add tenant-level queue metric and a small API change for `x-request-estimated-cost` header to help customers self-throttle.

ellis-oncall: closing channel for now, keep updates in the incident thread.

ops-bot: CloseNote: incident auto-closed at 2026-03-17T09:30:00Z (postmortem pending)
